proofs.full_local_argument: This paragraph is a local reconstruction, not a quotation. If r_0=0 the conclusion is immediate. Otherwise p_0=r_0!=0. Inductively suppose r_0,...,r_i are nonzero and orthogonal, p_0,...,p_i are nonzero and pairwise A-conjugate, their spans equal the corresponding residual spans at every prefix, and r_i is orthogonal to p_0,...,p_{i-1}. These hold at i=0. Since p_i=r_i+b_{i-1}p_{i-1} for i>0, (r_i,p_i)=|r_i|^2 (also true at i=0). Positive definiteness gives d_i=(p_i,A p_i)>0, so a_i=|r_i|^2/d_i>0. The x and r updates preserve r_{i+1}=k-Ax_{i+1}. Put s=r_{i+1}. For j<i, (s,p_j)=(r_i,p_j)-a_i(p_i,A p_j)=0 by symmetry/conjugacy; for j=i it equals |r_i|^2-a_i d_i=0. Thus s is orthogonal to every previous p_j and, by the prefix-span equality, to every r_j for j<=i. If s=0, stop. Otherwise let beta=|s|^2/|r_i|^2 and p_{i+1}=s+beta p_i. Because (s,p_i)=0, (s,p_{i+1})=|s|^2>0; thus p_{i+1}!=0 and the prefix spans remain equal. For j<i, the earlier residual updates give A p_j=(r_j-r_{j+1})/a_j. Hence (s,A p_j)=0, and (p_{i+1},A p_j)=0 using conjugacy of p_i. For j=i, (s,A p_i)=(s,r_i-s)/a_i=-|s|^2/a_i, while beta(p_i,A p_i)=|s|^2/a_i. Their sum is zero. This completes the induction. If stopping has not occurred before n updates, r_0,...,r_{n-1} are n nonzero orthogonal vectors and form a basis of R^n. The next residual r_n is orthogonal to that basis and is therefore zero. Thus the first zero has index m<=n. Since A is invertible, r_m=0 implies x_m=h. The displayed implementation uses one product per update and at most one for initialization, yielding m+1<=n+1; all other operations are separately counted in complexity_scope.

assumptions: A is real symmetric positive definite: z^T A z>0 for all z!=0.
All matrix-vector products, inner products, scalar and vector arithmetic and zero tests are exact.
Stop at the first zero residual; no division is performed using a zero residual or zero search direction.
statement.conclusion: The recurrence is well-defined until stopping: each continuing p_i is nonzero and p_i^T A p_i>0, and r_i=k-Ax_i. There exists a first m in {0,...,n} with r_m=0 and x_m=h. The nonzero residuals r_0,...,r_{m-1} are pairwise Euclidean-orthogonal, and p_0,...,p_{m-1} are pairwise A-conjugate. When r_0=0, m=0. At most n updates and at most n+1 matrix-vector products including the generic initialization product suffice.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let (u,v)=u^T v on R^n, A in R^{n x n}, k,x_0 in R^n and h=A^{-1}k. Initialize r_0=k-Ax_0, p_0=r_0. For i=0,1,... while r_i != 0, query q_i=A p_i; set rho_i=(r_i,r_i), a_i=rho_i/(p_i,q_i), x_{i+1}=x_i+a_i p_i, r_{i+1}=r_i-a_i q_i. If r_{i+1}=0 return x_{i+1}; otherwise b_i=(r_{i+1},r_{i+1})/rho_i and p_{i+1}=r_{i+1}+b_i p_i. Reuse q_i in both denominator and residual update.
statement.parameter_domains: n in positive integers; k and x_0 arbitrary real vectors; i is a nonnegative integer before stopping. No accuracy, spectral-gap or condition-number restriction.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every integer n>=1, every real SPD A of that dimension, every k and every x_0 in R^n, the deterministic sequence below has the stated properties; no randomness or generic-position assumption.
